source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Plug uart dongle to get data.
2.  Check bits per second  115200.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Output of console should be human readable
2. Should be able to control SUT in console mode via keyboard.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- BMC UART debugging: BMC UART debugging requires a physical serial console (USB-UART) attached to the BMC debug header; the agent has no physical UART and cannot observe the BMC boot/debug output over SSH.  [scenario: BMC-UART-debug (Debug Console set)]
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator captures the BMC UART serial-boot log; agent cannot produce serial capture over SSH. (context: BMC-UART-debug (Debug Console set))
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: physical debug UART operation is human-only; do not attempt via SSH.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO. It correctly preserves the required physical UART path and rejects SSH substitution, but does not address pinout/voltage or the risk of privileged keyboard input.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED. It retains 115200 bps and adds electrical validation, receive-first capture and explicit console-input scope.

original_test_intent: Verify that a physical BMC debug UART at 115200 bps produces human-readable console data and accepts approved keyboard input that controls the intended SUT console.
original_method: A qualified operator connects the correct USB-UART adapter to the verified BMC debug header, opens a terminal at 115200 with approved framing, captures receive output, and enters only safe approved keystrokes to demonstrate control.
manual_activity: A qualified operator must attach and later remove the physical adapter, verify wiring and electrical level, identify the serial device, judge human readability, and provide controlled keyboard input. SSH is not equivalent to this debug path.
required_inputs: BMC header location, pinout, ground and UART voltage level
Approved adapter/cable and exact 115200 framing, parity, stop-bit and flow-control settings
Console identity and bounded keyboard-input sequence that demonstrates control without reconfiguration
SUT/BMC power state, OOB recovery, operator and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Never guess the header, pin order, voltage or serial device; a mismatch can damage the BMC/board.
Begin receive-only and do not send input until the prompt/target and allowed command set are confirmed.
Stop on garbled data, wrong console, reset/configuration prompt, instability or OOB loss.
Preserve raw capture and logs, safely disconnect, and do not retry or alter baud/framing automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare terminal/capture settings after the operator establishes the approved physical connection.
Capture and checksum raw UART bytes with timestamps and analyze readability/response evidence.
Send only explicitly approved benign input under operator control, then collect post-health data without deciding PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Validate and make the physical UART connection and disconnection.
Approve the console target, framing and safe keyboard sequence.
Judge readability/control and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its no-SSH warning is correct, but it provides no terminal command and cannot complete the physical connection or keyboard criterion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After physical setup, use the project-approved serial capture application at exactly 115200 and supplied framing; do not guess `/dev/tty*`, COM port or terminal options.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Physical dongle, 115200 bps, readable output, keyboard control and both ten-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a timestamped raw binary/text capture from the validated serial port, start receive-only, record the prompt identity, then send a documented non-destructive input and capture the response.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the mapped BMC debug header and voltage-compatible adapter.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record adapter, USB-serial driver, terminal tool, BMC and board revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform schematic/service UART specification and approved terminal-tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds electrical validation, immutable capture and restricted input while retaining the physical 115200 path.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; a remote serial-over-LAN endpoint is not substituted unless the project separately proves it is the same path.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Pinout, voltage, framing, port and safe input.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Readable output alone does not prove transmit control; a recorded response to approved input is also required.

project_override_considerations: A project can choose its terminal application and benign control sequence, but must preserve the physical BMC UART path and 115200 bps. Missing adapter/settings are readiness inputs, not a reason to change the manual capability label to BLOCKED.
expected_evidence: Board/BMC/header identity, pinout, voltage, adapter and full serial settings
Timestamped raw capture showing human-readable output at 115200
Exact approved keyboard input and corresponding console response proving control
Pre/post BMC/SUT health, safe disconnect/restoration and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The physical dongle, baud rate and readable/control criteria are mutually consistent. Omitted framing and command scope are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The required adapter, wiring and approved input can be supplied by the project; the physical connection and judgment make the case MANUAL ONLY rather than permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree that the physical debug UART cannot be replaced by SSH, and add missing electrical and transmit-scope safeguards.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with MANUAL ONLY and preserve its receive-first, pinout and command-boundary controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates agent-assisted serial capture from the human physical connection and formal engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Turns a generic physical limitation into a safe, evidence-complete UART method that proves both receive readability and controlled transmit behavior.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source acceptance spans an electrical attachment and a bidirectional console interaction. Software can capture bytes only after the adapter is physically and correctly wired; it cannot validate pins or safely make that connection. Human readability and authorized control also require an operator-defined prompt/response, so MANUAL ONLY is accurate.

no_automatic_retry: Make one approved connection/capture/input attempt. On electrical, target, readability or response anomaly, stop input, retain the capture and disconnect safely; do not scan ports or change settings automatically.
